Prevention: Clean tillage- equipment and tools from infested fields so rhizomes and bulbs of the weed are not spread.
Adjust tillage direction to prevent spreading rhizomes and tubers from infested to uninfested field parts.
Avoid using crop weed residues from harvested infested fields as mulch since this contains weed seed.
Plant maize with the first rains at the recommended spacing, this is usually at 0.75m by 0.25m (one plant per station) for increased weed shading.
Rotate maize with soya bean as the latter suppresses the weed.
Monitoring: Yellow nutsedge is a grassy weed with thin triangular stems that favours low and poorly drained soils.
The weed is persistent and can grow up to 1m high.
It reduces maize yields through competition for nutrients, water and light.
The weed stem is free of nodes, leaves are thin and v-shaped with rhizome originating from underground rhizomes and tubers.
Look for underground roots with rhizomes that enlarge to form tubers.
Mature weeds have yellow flowers that produce a lot of seeds.
Consider mechanical control if the density is 2 to 4 plants/ m 2 for young weeds and 1 to 3 plants/ m for old weeds.
Consider chemical control if the density is 8 to 10 plants/ m 2 for young weeds and 2 to 5 plants/ m for old weeds.
Direct Control: Till the land with mouldboard plough to expose the rhizomes and tubers to sunlight.
Use secondary tillage that will shred the rhizomes and tubers.
Where a hand hoe is used, dig out rhizomes & tubers and expose them to sunlight for fast drying.
Weed as soon as the threshold is reached, until the crop canopy closes.
Weed regularly to allow the maize crop to shade the yellow nutsedge regrowth.
S-metolachlor-products (chloroacetamide herbicide group) using a knapsack sprayer after the first rains but before maize emerges.
Followed by spraying of post-emergent glyphosate (organophosphate) with nonaoic acid as spot spray using sprayer with nozzle shield after weed re- emergence.
Uttermost care must be exercised to avoid killing the maize even with the nozzle shield.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.

Avoid spraying the herbicide on maize by use of a nozzle shield.
Any herbicide drift will kill the maize.
